Occurrences.Kwic: 若教伊踏著德山、臨濟門下，免見九年冷坐，被人喚作壁觀胡僧。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X79/X79n1557.xml). Joint Essentials of the Lamps: Tianyi Yihuai says that had Bodhidharma met the Deshan or Linji gate he might have avoided nine years of cold sitting and being called the wall-gazing foreign monk.

Senses.Explanation: Wall-gazing is the name used by the corpus for facing a wall in sustained silent observation, above all in the Shaolin biography of Bodhidharma. Chan records also treat the label as contestable: Zhongfeng lists deadened posture and darkened mind as one disputed account of Chan, while Tianyi calls the nine years attributed to Bodhidharma “cold sitting.” The lamp biography supplies the ordinary scene rather than an imported system: Bodhidharma sits facing the wall all day in silence and people call him the wall-gazing brahmin. A parallel lamp record repeats that scene. A transmitted introduction explicitly equates its described settling of mind with wall-gazing and distinguishes it from four conducts. Dahui calls closing the gate and wall-gazing medicine for quieting the mind in one letter. The negative controls are equally explicit. Zhongfeng includes deadened resolve and darkening the mind among rival claims about Chan, and Tianyi says Deshan or Linji might have spared Bodhidharma nine years of cold sitting and the wall-gazing label. The corpus does not supply numbered steps, prescribed duration for students, breath directions, or a wall-gazing manual. The entry therefore names the observed wall-facing scene and its contested Chan deployment without turning it into a standardized exercise.
